Bio link is broken mid-URL across lines as "https://opencollective.com /tusky", a visibly mangled label.
verdicts.notes: A is the only screen that even attempts the brief, and it lands the two hardest parts: "Sert à faire remonter des bourses auxquelles tu pourrais être admissible. Jamais partagé ni vendu." says exactly what tags unlock, and the delete card states the consequence and the second step before you touch it. Its honesty is the weak seam — "CONFIRMÉE" in the sticky header versus "celle que tu as saisie" in the footer is a contradiction a student would notice, and "Préparer ma rencontre" is a full-width button that says nothing about what happens next. B is a competent shipped screen but it is someone else's public profile, not a self-service account screen, and its FAB-over-text and split URLs are sloppier than anything in A.

verdicts.gapA: A never shows a notifications surface at all: the body is an "Appearance" list ("App" → "Theme / Selected: Light theme", "Dynamic colors", "Language / System default"; "Entries" → "View mode", "Show icons", "Code digit grouping"), with no notification toggles, no per-row consequence copy, and no guest/signed-in state anywhere; on top of that the screen is a store-listing composite — half the canvas is spent on the marketing lockup "Customizable / Many customization options, encryption and backups" and the device frame crops the last row, "Show the account name", mid-cell at the bottom edge. Replacing the marketing frame with the actual four-toggle notifications list plus a signed-out explainer is what would move my pick.
verdicts.gapB: The header strip is the weakest region: "COTE R" wraps onto two lines ("COTE" over "R") beside "31,20 CONFIRMÉE", and that figure sits with no source or verification date next to it — the only reassurance is 1,900px away in the footnote "Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie… Chaque seuil, date et bourse affiché porte sa source et sa date de vérification." Putting "saisie par toi · vérifiée le …" (or the equivalent) directly against the 31,20 and un-wrapping the label would close it; secondarily, all four toggles read identically grey/off, so nothing distinguishes "off by choice" from "locked while signed out" despite the card saying "Enregistré sur cet appareil."
violationsA: Truncated/clipped row: the bottom row "Show the account name" is cut off mid-cell by the device-frame edge, with its supporting line missing entirely
violationsB: Displayed figure without adjacent source/verification date: header reads "COTE R 31,20 CONFIRMÉE" with the provenance only in a distant footer note, and the word "CONFIRMÉE" next to it reads as a verified figure
verdicts.notes: B is the only screen that even attempts the brief and largely lands it: four rows each explain their trigger in plain language ("Dès qu'un seuil officiel d'admission change pour l'un de tes programmes cibles"), the guest state is stated as a consequence rather than a warning ("Enregistré sur cet appareil. Connecte-toi pour retrouver ces choix sur tes autres appareils.") with a real 56px "Me connecter" target, and no push/permission block appears — consistent with the key-gated rule. Its craft faults are real but local: the cramped header lockup, a dead ~130px band between the sign-in card and the footer, and toggles whose off-state carries no label. A is a marketing composite of a different settings screen; it fails the criterion outright rather than executing it imperfectly.

verdicts.gapA: A is not a working list screen at all: the top ~30% is marketing copy ("Customize the Explore feed to show things that interest you") over a device mockup, and the feed inside it is a generic Wikipedia Explore stream with no sections, no match reasons and clipped rows — the first row "MORE LIKE THIS" is orphaned from a card whose header is above the crop, and the last card ("Featured article… Echo parakeet / Species of parrot endemic to Mauritius") is sliced by the phone frame. Closing this means replacing the promo frame with a real full-bleed sectioned list whose rows say why each item is there; nothing smaller would move my pick.
verdicts.gapB: In the "Admissible maintenant" section, the "Bourses Perspective Québec (TI, Génie, Santé, Éducation)" card has no why-chip row at all — it jumps from "Gouvernement du Québec (MES) 2 500 $ – 20 000 $" straight to the divider, "28 février 2027" and "Postuler", so the card with the widest amount range is the one that never says why it matched. Every sibling card carries chips ("Ton cégep", "Ton programme", "Ta cote R", "Étiquette : Leadership", "Ouvert à tous"), which makes the omission read as a data hole rather than a design choice. Secondary but related: "Ta cote R" as a bare chip says far less than the good pattern one section down, "Cote min. 32,0 : à 0,8 de ta cote".
violationsA: Truncated/clipped content: the top row "MORE LIKE THIS" is severed from its card, and the bottom card ("Echo parakeet / Species of parrot endemic to Mauritius") is cut mid-content by the mockup frame
Displayed dates carry no source or verification stamp: "Main page on 25 Jun 2019" in the green Today on Wikipedia block and "20 Jun 2019" in the Featured article header
Affordance/target: the only per-card controls are 3-dot kebab glyphs ("VIEW MAIN PAGE ⋮", "ROLL THE DICE ⋮"), tiny hit areas with no visible button shape
violationsB: Touch target: the "source" pill in every card footer ("Vérifié le 24 août 2026 · source") measures ~44×90 device px, i.e. roughly 22×45 CSS px at 2x — half the 44px minimum, while framed as a tappable bordered chip (repeated on all 12 cards)

Honesty of a figure: the header states "COTE R 31,20 CONFIRMÉE" with no source or verification date beside it, and the only disclaimer that it is self-entered ("Ta cote R est celle que tu as saisie") sits ~8000px away in the footer, so the badge "CONFIRMÉE" can be read as an official confirmation
verdicts.notes: B is the only one of the two that is a screen doing a job: three visibly distinct section headers (green "Admissible maintenant", rust "À portée", grey "À explorer"), per-card source and verification date, and honest dead-ends ("Aucune date limite publiée", "Pas de formulaire en ligne. Contacte les services aux étudiants de ton cégep.") instead of invented deadlines. Its craft is sound — amount in blue as the second read after the title, 48px "Postuler" pills, consistent card rhythm — and I found no out-of-region rows and no copy ranking careers or predicting admission. A is a store-listing promo image, not a screen, so the comparison is not close.
